correctness.rationale: For any finite projective plane of order q>=2, graph distances force the scale-four Čech nerve to equal the union of two explicit cones, whose intersection is exactly the join of the collinearity and concurrency complexes. Distinct line simplices intersect only in vertices; the explicit descending-cardinality free-face sequence collapses each to a star tree without shared-face interference. Each resulting graph has v=q^2+q+1 vertices, qv edges and cycle rank (q-1)v+1=q^3. Standard homotopy pushout and join identities give a wedge of q^6 four-spheres, proving integral homology without field extrapolation. The package verifier checks all axioms, facets and factor collapses at q=2,3; for q=2 it also checks all 7919 faces, intersection join and mod-two ranks. Limits: finite verification alone does not cover other orders; uniform proof does.

originality.rationale: No inspected source states or implies the order-uniform homotopy classification of scale-four intrinsic Čech nerves for finite projective-plane incidence graphs. The 2022 Čech source proves the general ball-neighborhood facet rule and analyzes hypercubes; the 2014 D-neighborhood thesis defines the construction and analyzes other families. The closest published projective-plane incidence result determines a scale-two Vietoris–Rips flag complex, not this Čech nerve. A previously recorded Heawood evaluation is the special case of order two only; the new theorem covers every existing order, and therefore cannot follow from that finite case. Results of semantic and web searches limit but do not certify originality.

value.rationale: Projective-plane incidence graphs are a canonical unbounded family of diameter-three bipartite metric graphs, including non-Desarguesian examples. The exact rank q^6 in degree four grows with order while the simplicial dimension (q+1)^2 also grows, showing a strong collapse of apparent dimension and a precise squaring of the two collinearity cycle ranks. The claim gives a natural complete homotopy classification and integral torsion-freeness for an entire graph Čech scale; it is not a recomputation of a known fixed graph or a generic graph lemma. The single-order Heawood specialization is credited as a check, not the source of novelty.
